data.name: Mahoor
data.gender_notes: Mahoor is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘mahwa’ which means ‘to forgive’. In Islamic tradition, the name Mahoor symbolizes the forgiven and the compassionate. The name Mahoor carries the meaning “The Forgiven One” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mahoor usually hope their child will grow to embody the forgiven one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes forgiveness and compassion in Islam.
data.etymology: Mahoor belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Forgiven One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mahoor total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah (The Beginning and the End) - Vol. VIII, Page 116-117. This book is a classic and authoritative work on Islamic history.
historical_references.context: Mahoor ibn Masruq Al-Thaqafi was a famous poet, who wrote poems in praise of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his companions. He was also a Sahabi (Companion) of the Prophet, and was present at the Battle of Uhud. He was martyred at the age of 35 while defending Madinah against the invading Byzantine and Ghassanid forces during the Battle of Mu'tah.

historical_references.reference: Al-Tabari's The History of al-Tabari - Vol. II, Page 167-168. This book is another important work on Islamic history.
historical_references.context: Mahoor ibn Masruq Al-Thaqafi was also a close companion of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the fourth Caliph of Islam. He accompanied Ali on his military campaigns and was one of his most trusted advisors. During the Battle of the Camel, Mahoor was martyred at the age of 40 while defending Ali against the forces of Aisha bint Abu Bakr.
